{{Short description|Construction in commutative algebra}}
In [[commutative algebra]], the '''Rees algebra''' or '''Rees ring''' of an [[ideal of a ring|ideal]] ''I'' in a [[commutative ring]] ''R'' is defined to be <blockquote><math>R[It]=\bigoplus_{n=0}^{\infty} I^n t^{n}\subseteq R[t].</math></blockquote>
The '''extended Rees algebra''' of ''I'' (which some authors<ref>{{Cite book|title = Commutative Algebra with a View Toward Algebraic Geometry|last = Eisenbud|first = David|publisher = Springer-Verlag|year = 1995|isbn = 978-3-540-78122-6}}</ref> refer to as the Rees algebra of ''I'') is defined as<blockquote><math>R[It,t^{-1}]=\bigoplus_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}I^nt^{n}\subseteq R[t,t^{-1}].</math></blockquote>This construction has special interest in [[algebraic geometry]] since the [[Proj_construction|projective scheme]] defined by the Rees algebra of an ideal in a ring is the [[Blowing_up|blowing-up]] of the [[spectrum of a ring|spectrum]] of the ring along the [[subscheme]] defined by the ideal (see {{section link|Ideal sheaf|Algebraic geometry}}).<ref>Eisenbud-Harris, ''The geometry of schemes''. Springer-Verlag, 197, 2000</ref>

== Properties ==

The Rees algebra is an algebra over <math>\mathbb{Z}[t^{-1}]</math>, and it is defined so that, quotienting by <math>t^{-1}=0</math> or ''t=λ'' for ''λ'' any invertible element in ''R'',  we get <blockquote><math>\text{gr}_I R \ \leftarrow\ R[It]\ \to\ R.</math></blockquote>
Thus it interpolates between ''R'' and its associated graded ring ''gr<sub>I</sub>R''. 

* Assume ''R'' is [[Noetherian ring|Noetherian]]; then ''R[It]'' is also Noetherian.  The [[Krull dimension]] of the Rees algebra is <math>\dim R[It]=\dim R+1</math> if ''I'' is not contained in any [[prime ideal]] ''P'' with <math>\dim(R/P)=\dim R</math>; otherwise <math>\dim R[It]=\dim R</math>. The Krull dimension of the extended Rees algebra is <math>\dim R[It, t^{-1}]=\dim R+1</math>.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title = Integral Closure of Ideals, Rings, and Modules|last = Swanson|first = Irena|author1-link= Irena Swanson |publisher = Cambridge University Press|year = 2006|isbn = 9780521688604|last2 = Huneke|first2 = Craig}}</ref>
* If <math>J\subseteq I</math> are ideals in a Noetherian ring ''R'', then the ring extension <math>R[Jt]\subseteq R[It]</math> is [[Integral extension|integral]] if and only if ''J'' is a reduction of ''I''.<ref name=":0" />
* If ''I'' is an ideal in a Noetherian ring ''R'', then the Rees algebra of ''I'' is the [[Quotient ring|quotient]] of the [[symmetric algebra]] of ''I'' by its [[Torsion (algebra)|torsion]] submodule.

== Relationship with other blow-up algebras ==
The [[associated graded ring]] of ''I'' may be defined as<blockquote><math>\operatorname{gr}_I(R)=R[It]/IR[It].</math></blockquote>If ''R'' is a Noetherian [[local ring]] with maximal ideal <math>\mathfrak{m}</math>, then the [[special fiber ring]] of ''I'' is given by<blockquote><math>\mathcal{F}_I(R)=R[It]/\mathfrak{m}R[It].</math></blockquote>The Krull dimension of the special fiber ring is called the [[analytic spread]] of ''I''.
